report.summary: Reviewed chunk 4 of 5 of vendors.py: AntigravityAdapter, OllamaAdapter, VendorAvailability dataclass, available_vendors function. Claims checked against visible code.
risks: AntigravityAdapter._dispatch | medium | Returns 'not_authenticated' without probing; relies on operator assertion. | Add a test with signed_in=False to confirm immediate return.
OllamaAdapter.__init__ | medium | local property computed from lane_for_host; could disagree with lane if host is loopback but lane is 'untrusted'. | Verify lane_for_host logic consistency.
available_vendors | medium | agy availability depends on agy_signed_in flag; no probe for actual auth. | Confirm that operator must set flag correctly.

claims.text: The prompt goes on STDIN (``agy -p -``) and NEVER on a command line.
claims.why: argv() builds command with '-p', '-'; prompt passed via stdin_text in _dispatch.

claims.text: ``ssh`` with a trailing command does not take an argv: it concatenates its arguments and hands the string to the REMOTE login shell, which re-parses it.
claims.why: argv() returns list of strings; subprocess.run() uses list, but SSH on remote side concatenates. The code passes arguments as list to subprocess, which is correct for local argv, but remote shell will re-parse. Claim is accurate about SSH behavior.

claims.text: The prompt here is a diff written by a candidate model, so an ordinary patch containing backticks or ``$(...)`` -- a shell script, a test log, a Python f-string -- would execute on the bench as Administrator, with no adversarial model required.
claims.why: The docstring describes a security risk; code does not implement any sanitization. Claim is about external behavior, not verifiable from code alone.

claims.text: Local ``subprocess`` argv quoting cannot help: the escaping that matters belongs to a shell we cannot see.
claims.why: argv() uses a list, which subprocess passes correctly to local exec, but SSH concatenates; remote shell re-parses. The code does not add any quoting.

claims.text: ``agy`` has not completed its one-time interactive sign-in on this machine, so this adapter is DISABLED BY DEFAULT: it reports ``unavailable`` / ``not_authenticated`` immediately rather than hanging on an auth prompt.
claims.why: __init__ sets signed_in=False by default; _dispatch returns unavailable with reason not_authenticated when signed_in is False.

claims.text: An operator asserts sign-in with ``signed_in=True``; nothing here probes it, because probing means invoking a model.
claims.why: signed_in is a boolean flag; _dispatch does not probe auth, only checks the flag.

claims.text: The host is passed EXPLICITLY per call.  ``OLLAMA_HOST`` is never read for routing and never written
claims.why: Code does not reference OLLAMA_HOST; host parameter is used. Claim about never reading OLLAMA_HOST cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: ``local`` is ``sensitivity.lane_for_host(host) == "trusted"`` -- numeric loopback only, the same predicate that decides the egress lane, so the two cannot disagree about one host.
claims.why: __init__ sets self.local = lane_for_host(self.host) == 'trusted'. This matches the claim.

claims.text: Over-budget prompts are REFUSED LOUDLY.  Ollama HEAD-truncates an over-long prompt -- it eats the system prompt first -- so a silently truncated council turn is a reviewer that never saw the question it is answering.
claims.why: _dispatch checks tokens > window and returns error with over_context_budget reason before calling chat.

claims.text: The budget is ``_ollama_native.effective_input_window()`` (full ``num_ctx`` minus the generation reserve), reused rather than reinvented.
claims.why: effective_input_window is imported; its implementation is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Deliberately NOT keyed on host: local 7b and bench 7b are the same weights, so they must collide as one class.
claims.why: independence_class returns ('local', model_family(self.model)); host is not included.

claims.text: ONE predicate, shared with the egress gate it feeds. Not a local copy: ``local`` and ``lane`` must never be able to disagree about the same host, and they did (``[::1]`` was local-but-untrusted).
claims.why: self.local is computed from lane_for_host; lane is set to 'trusted' by default. The comment references a past bug; code now uses shared predicate.

claims.text: Cheap probe result.  No model is invoked to produce this.
claims.why: Dataclass fields are static; available_vendors uses which() and http_probe() only.

claims.text: Which vendors could be seated, established by CHEAP PROBES ONLY. Does the binary exist; does the Ollama host answer ``/api/version``.  No model is invoked, no prompt is sent, nothing is billed.  ``agy`` is reported unavailable until an operator asserts sign-in: the only way to test its auth is to call it, and a probe that calls a model is not a probe.
claims.why: Function calls which() and http_probe(); for agy, uses agy_signed_in flag. No model calls.

claims.text: Both callables are injectable so a test can establish availability with no CLI on PATH and no network.
claims.why: which and http_probe are parameters with defaults; tests can inject mocks.

observations.what: AntigravityAdapter._auth_failure checks returncode and _looks_unauthenticated; but _dispatch also checks _looks_unauthenticated on blob. There is duplicate logic.
OllamaAdapter._dispatch uses effective_input_window() and count_tokens() without explicit import visible; they are presumably imported at module top.
available_vendors constructs VendorAvailability for agy with endpoint f'ssh:{BENCH_SSH_TARGET.split('@')[-1]}'; but BENCH_SSH_TARGET is not defined in this chunk.
available_vendors uses COUNCIL_PROFILES dict but it is not defined in this chunk; likely imported.
